digest.component_or_area: plan-review attestation and material basis hashing
propositions: Attestation staleness messages name a fixed fictional list (description/AC/file_impact/children) instead of revealing which component actually changed, preventing operators from diagnosing the cause.

Ticking AC checkboxes does not invalidate attestations because _normalize_checkbox_state normalizes checkbox state before hashing, but pre-330c attestations hashed raw descriptions and can read as stale when boxes are later unticked.

The material basis is a composite SHA256 over exactly four keys (ticket_id, description, file_impact, children) plus file_impact_scope when scope is none; per-component hashes must be extracted and stored in the signed manifest to enable diagnostic blame.

Attestation refusal surfaces across generation.py, resign.py, completion.py, attest_gate.py, and _cli/_llm_commands.py either omit the reason or forward a generic fixed list, preventing users from taking corrective action.

Legacy pre-330c attestations cannot be unambiguously distinguished from current ones at read time without replaying the event store to signed_at, which is infeasible because children derive from other tickets' state and compaction squashes legacy events.
